title: On the Theology of Plato
author: Proclus

source_edition.statement: The Six Books of Proclus on the Theology of Plato, translated from the Greek, to which a seventh book is added in order to supply the deficiency of another book on this subject which was written by Proclus but since lost, by Thomas Taylor, 2 vols (London: printed for the author, 1816). This edition serves the Theology of Plato alone, over the two volumes the print gives it: vol. I entire, and vol. II only as far as the Theology runs in it (its printed pages 1-299). It stops there deliberately, and the printed volume does not: vol. II's next work is the Elements of Theology (its printed pages 301-441), which is a work of its own and already has its own edition in this library, and the treatises follow the Elements (On Providence and Fate, the Ten Doubts concerning Providence, and the Subsistence of Evil). Carrying vol. II on to the treatises would not serve this work; it would serve a second work twice.

items.role: the volume's preliminaries: the title page, Taylor's Introduction, and the explanatory glossary that closes it (archive leaves n0-n75)
vol. I, the work entire (printed pp. 1-425, to Book V ch. XXXIX)
vol. II, the Theology alone (printed pp. 1-299, Books VI-VII to the work's close CHAP. LI)

scan_source.note: ONE archive item, TWO printed volumes of the work -- re-sourced 2026-10-05. Taylor's 1816 edition divides the work over two volumes (vol. I printed pp. 1-425 to Book V ch. XXXIX; vol. II printed pp. 1-299, Books VI-VII to the work's close), and BOTH are bound in one scanned item, `thomastaylor`, so the scans are that one item's own leaves over the two runs of pages the work occupies in it: v1-n76.jpg .. v1-n500.jpg and v2-n506.jpg .. v2-n804.jpg. The stored leaf file names carry the VOLUME prefix because the two runs are the two halves of one work whose pages restart at 1 in vol. II, and because a rule's evidence file/url is written the same way; the ITEM is the same for both, and `items[]` says so. The item's next work begins at n805 (the Elements of Theology, printed pp. 301-441 -- its own edition in this library, cut from this same item at n806-n946), so the leaves after n804 belong to another work. The measured leaf arithmetic, verified at both ends of each run, is in the edition's scan.json, which this record summarises. The FRONT MATTER of vol. I is recorded as its own entry with NO offset and no printed-page range: archive leaves n0-n75 carry the title page, Taylor's Introduction and its glossary, and the only page numbers on them are ROMAN (leaf 74 reads 'Ixxix', leaf 75 'Ixxx'), so the page model computes no printed page for them -- see scan.json. Those leaves are held because the transcription opens on them and 339 of the finder's Greek runs stand there.
